name: Clonnach

attributes.attribute: appears in later oral tales of the Crom Dubh family

text: Clonnach is a mythological figure, introduced as a son of Crom Crnaich in later oral tales. In those stories the father no longer appears as an idol or a god. He takes the shape of Crom Dubh, a pagan chief who stands against St Patrick. This shift shows how later oral tradition recast old mythic figures into human opponents of the saint.

okr.objective: Clonnach is the son of Crom Crnaich in later tales where the father is Crom Dubh.
key_results: Clonnach is named as a son of Crom Crnaich, chiefly in tales passed down by word of mouth.
In those later tellings the father is no idol or god but Crom Dubh, a pagan chief who resists St Patrick.
okr.evidence: MacKillop, Dictionary of Celtic Mythology, s.v. Clonnach
